subject: Arcadia-v2 latency anomaly / SLA exception request
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novabank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency jump after Arcadia-v2 rollout (p95 ~ 1.2s)

Hi Jordan,

We're seeing a pronounced latency regression on the Arcadia-v2 model since your rollout this morning. Our production p95 for /nlp/invoice-route has jumped from ~450ms to ~1.15-1.3s over the last two hours; p50 is mostly unchanged. This is affecting our synchronous payment authorization flow and causing some timeouts.

Key details:
- Route: /nlp/invoice-route (sync)
- Region: us-east-1
- Onset: ~07:05 PDT after a staggered feature-flag flip to arcadia-v2
- Observed: p50 190ms, p95 1.2s, error rate up 0.1% (mostly timeouts)

We need an urgent mitigation — either pin traffic back to Arcadia-v1 or a rollback. We also require formal SLA exception documentation and any compensatory credit discussion if this persists. I've attached a short screenshot from our monitoring and a sample trace.

Please advise next steps and an ETA for a mitigation plan. We're prepared to divert traffic if you authorize the rollback.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Reliability
NovaBank

Attachments: sample_trace.json (sent separately), quick_perf_screenshot.png
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novabank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency jump after Arcadia-v2 rollout (p95 ~ 1.2s)

Elena — thanks for the quick heads up and the trace. Sorry you're seeing this.

We've opened INF-7891 and our on-call serving team is looking at the perf deltas now. Initial ask: can you send a short HAR or a sample request id on one of the slow traces? that'll help isolate whether request sizes or KV cache warming are involved.

Short-term mitigations we're prepared to execute (need your approval):
- Provisional traffic pin to arcadia-v1 for the /nlp/invoice-route only (will keep other routes on v2)
- Activate a 48-hour SLA exception window while we triage; we will provide a post-incident report and proposed credit if SLA breach is confirmed
- Run a targeted canary rollback for Arcadia-v2 (staged -> full rollback) using the rollback-playbook.md (attached)

If you authorize the pin/rollback, we'll schedule a 30-minute incident coordination call and trigger the rollback playbook. Please confirm: 1) pin-only to v1 for invoice-route? 2) do you want full rollback across all routes?

-Jordan

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Sudden latency jump after Arcadia-v2 rollout (p95 ~ 1.2s)

Team — quick status and proposal from platform/ops: we've reproduced the p95 tail increase in our canary telemetry for the same route with similar traffic shape. Early signal points to a KV cache miss pattern and a kernel scheduling regression on a specific GPU driver combo when sequence lengths exceed ~420 tokens.

Proposed immediate action (we can execute within 20 minutes after approval):
1) Apply traffic pin for /nlp/invoice-route -> arcadia-v1 (routing rule change only; no infra churn).
2) Open provisional SLA exception for 48 hours (we'll log start/end times and metric deltas).
3) Run staged rollback for arcadia-v2 per rollback-playbook.md: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% OR abort after any p95 regression persists at canary.
4) Collect artifacts: arcadia_v2_perf_graph.png, arcadia_v2_kv_cache_dump.txt, full trace bundle. Attachments linked below.

Notes on risk: pinning to v1 for a single route has low blast radius; a full rollback across all routes is higher-risk for user-visible regressions in other pipelines. Prefer route-scoped pin first to buy time.

Approval requests: Jordan, can you get customer confirmation for route-scoped pin? Ben, open a legal ticket for SLA exception language/credits (we'll need to pre-authorize a provisional credit cap). Marissa, prepare the incident postmortem template and the customer-facing summary.

-Kim

Attachments: rollback-playbook.md, arcadia_v2_perf_graph.png, arcadia_v2_kv_cache_dump.txt
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novabank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Arcadia-v2 latency anomaly / SLA exception request

Elena — thanks for the sample trace. NovaBank confirmed: proceed with the route-scoped pin to Arcadia-v1 for /nlp/invoice-route only. Please consider this email the customer's authorization.

Actions taken / next steps:
- Routing rule applied at 16:20 PDT (pin to arcadia-v1 for invoice-route). Visible p95 fell back to ~460ms within two minutes.
- INF-7891 updated with artifacts and initial RCA notes; attached is the rollback-playbook.md and our perf graph.
- Ben, please open the legal ticket (LG-2264) to draft provisional credit language tied to the 48-hour window; cap requested: USD 15,000 pre-authorized.
- Marissa, please draft the customer-facing incident summary; target delivery within 6 hours.
- Scheduling: 30-minute incident sync at 17:00 PDT today — invite sent to on-call, NovaBank, and SE.

I'll follow up with the post-incident report and the root cause once we complete the deeper traceback. Thanks everyone for the quick response.

-Jordan
